LESSON: WRITING 2.3.2 PRE-WRITING SKILLS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Writing 2.3.2 Pre-writing skills
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.3.2 Pre-writing skills, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: how to color for pleasure. ● In groups or pairs, learner is guided to sign sing songs on how to color. 1. Which materials do you use when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.3.2 Pre-writing skills together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Responsibility:Resilience as the learner practices writing by correctly holding a writing tool and scribbling.

• Integrity: Honesty as the learner does own work and displays it for feedback without seeking assistance from others.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Health related issues: personal hygiene as the learner washes hands after coloring with crayons.

Child safety and security as the learner follows simple teacher given rules not to eat color pencils and crayons and other writing

materials.

Link to other Learning Areas:

As learner models, to enhance pre writing activities they interact with creative activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as hearing aids and amplifiers, crayons, drawing books, tracing books,

sand tray, sand, modelling clay, objects of different sizes.
